newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar condemns Israeli settlement policy.
newsitem.headline: Qatar condemns Israeli settlement policy.

text.p: The Gulf Arab state of Qatar on Saturday condemned Israel's building of a controversial Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, saying the move threatened to unleash more bloodshed in the Middle East.

"Qatar had repeatedly warned of the dangers of the Israeli settlement policy in Jerusalem and occupied Arab lands...," the official Qatari News Agency (QNA) quoted foreign ministry spokesman Fawaz bin Ahmed al-Attiyah as saying.
He said Jewish settlements "threatened to return the region to an atmosphere of tension and violence such as the Tel Aviv cafe bombing which claimed innocent lives."

The attack on Friday, claimed by the militant Moslem group Hamas, killed three Israeli women. Hamas in a statement on Saturday threatened further attacks against Israel if the Jewish state continued to build the settlement.

Israel's groundbreaking on Tuesday to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a pine-covered hill between Jerusalem and the West Bank town of Bethlehem, occupied in the 1967 Middle East War, drew international condemnation and Palestinian rage.

On Saturday fierce Israeli-Arab clashes broke out in the West Bank town of Hebron, with Israeli soldiers firing live ammunition, rubber bullets and teargas at hundreds of Arab protesters who threw petrrol bombs and rocks.
Qatar, along with Oman, has reaced ahead of other Gulf Arab states in establishing open economic ties with Israel but stopped short of diplomatic ties pending resolution of the Arab-Israeli conflict.
